dedupe_keys.name: openfda food enforcement reports food recalls

description: The openFDA food enforcement API publishes every food recall reported to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration since 2004. Each record gives the recall number and event, its classification by hazard level (Class I to III), status, the product description and quantity, the reason for recall (such as Listeria, undeclared allergens or foreign objects), the recalling firm and address, the distribution pattern, whether it was voluntary or mandated, and the key dates. The producer is the FDA, drawing on its Recall Enterprise System; openFDA renames some fields and serves them as JSON. Coverage is national, with 29,415 records as of 16 September 2026, updated weekly. Data are free through the API (with a free key for higher rate limits) and as bulk downloads, dedicated to the public domain under Creative Commons CC0. Caveats: only FDA-regulated foods are included (meat, poultry and egg products are recalled by USDA FSIS), distribution areas are free text, and records describe regulatory events, not illness counts. Simulation uses: event data on contamination and supply interruptions for food supply chain disruption and cascading failure models, and on how widely products are distributed. Related records: the WFP food prices (data-wfp-global-food-prices) show market effects of larger shocks.
name: openFDA food enforcement reports (food recalls)
schema_summary: Per recall: recall number, event id, status, classification (I, II, III), product type and description, quantity, reason for recall, recalling firm and address, distribution pattern, voluntary or mandated, initiation, classification, report and termination dates, code information
